title: Score de Duke sur tapis roulant (Duke Treadmill score)
short_title: Score de Duke sur tapis roulant (Duke Treadmill score)
formula:
Duke Treadmill Score = duration of exercise, minutes – (5 × maximal net ST-segment deviation during or after exercise*, millimeters) – (4 × treadmill angina index)

* *except in lead aVR*

Where angina index is as follows:

| Feature | Angina Index |
| --- | --- |
| No angina during exercise | 0 |
| Non-limiting angina | 1 |
| Patient stops exercising because of angina | 2 |

how_to_use.why: Peut fournir des informations diagnostiques et pronostiques chez les patients chez qui une maladie coronarienne est suspectée, sur la base de l’épreuve d’effort sur tapis roulant.
how_to_use.when: Patients without known coronary artery disease undergoing treadmill EKG testing.
how_to_use.pearls:
- À utiliser avec prudence chez les patients évalués selon d'autres protocoles.
-
- Si un autre protocole est utilisé, envisager l'équivalent en multiples de la consommation d'oxygène de repos (METs) plutôt qu'en minutes d'effort.
- Fournit une information pronostique indépendante, en complément de l'anatomie coronaire, de la fraction d'éjection ventriculaire gauche et des données cliniques.
- Utilité incertaine en présence de l'un des éléments suivants : valvulopathie ou cardiopathie congénitale significative, antécédent de chirurgie cardiaque, ECG non interprétable en raison d'un bloc de branche gauche, sus-décalage du segment ST dans des dérivations comportant des ondes Q pathologiques.
- Ne prend pas en compte les variables cliniques telles que l'âge, la fréquence cardiaque ou la pression artérielle, qui sont des facteurs de risque connus de coronaropathie.

next_steps.advice:
- Based on score results, clinicians may decide to proceed with cardiac catheterization for suspected coronary artery disease.
- The[1997 ACC/AHA Guidelines for Exercise Testing](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/9207652)and[2012 ACCF/AHA/ACP/AATS/PCNA/SCAI/STS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Patients With Stable Ischemic Heart Disease](https://circ.ahajournals.org/content/126/25/e354)state that the Duke Treadmill Score is a validated tool for risk assessment for coronary artery disease.
- The[1997 ACC/AHA Guidelines for Exercise Testing](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/9207652)state if a patient has an exercise stress test with a high risk Duke Treadmill Score (<-10), coronary angiography should be considered.

evidence:
Derivation study,[Mark 1987](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/3579066):

- 2,842 patients referred to Duke University Medical Center between 1969 and 1980 with chest pain who had an exercise treadmill test (Bruce protocol) within 6 weeks of cardiac catheterization.
- Population randomly divided into two groups of equal size; Cox regression model was used in one to create the treadmill score that was validated in the other group.
- Exclusion: significant valvular or congenital heart disease, previous cardiac surgery, uninterpretable EKG due to LBBB, ST-segment elevation in leads with pathologic Q waves.
- The DTS adds independent prognostic information in addition to coronary anatomy, left ventricular ejection fraction, and clinical data.
- The treadmill score was useful to stratify prognosis in suspected coronary artery disease.

Validation study,[Mark 1991](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJM199109193251204):

- 613 outpatients.
- Prospective study.
- Predicted outcomes based on the Duke Treadmill Score agreed closely with observed outcomes at four years of follow-up.
more_info:
Interpretation:

| Duke Treadmill Score | Risk Group | Survival at 5 Years* |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ≥+5 | Low | 99% |
| -10 to +4 | Medium | 95% |
| <-10 | High | 79% |

*For outpatients. From[Mark 1991](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJM199109193251204).

![](https://cdn-web-img.mdcalc.com/content/dts.jpg)

The data from the treadmill exercise test can be plotted on a nomogram to derive an estimate of five-year survival or average annual mortality.

Prognosis is determined in five steps:

1. The observed amount of exercise-induced ST-segment deviation (the largest elevation or depression after resting changes have been subtracted) is marked on the line for ST-segment deviation during exercise.
2. The observed degree of angina during exercise is marked on the line for angina.
3. The marks for ST-segment deviation and degree of angina are connected with a straight edge. The point where this line intersects the ischemia-reading line is noted.
4. The total number of minutes of exercise in treadmill testing according to the Bruce protocol (or the equivalent in multiples of resting oxygen consumption [METs] from an alternative protocol) is marked on the exercise-duration line.
5. The mark for ischemia is connected with that for exercise duration. The point at which this line intersects the line for prognosis indicates the five-year survival rate and average annual mortality for patients with these characteristics.
